page: Amazon Web Services m6a.xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It features an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it does not include any GPUs. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results reveal a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance exhibits strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng, Geekbench, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also rank in the bottom 25%, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-intensive operations. Text processing and single-threaded compression tasks perform at average levels, while database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are relatively weak.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the m6a.xlarge offers a balanced resource density for general-purpose workloads that do not require high-performance multi-core scaling or high memory bandwidth. Given its strong single-core performance but weaker multi-core and database benchmarks, this instance is best suited for light web serving, single-threaded application tasks, basic text processing, and general-purpose development environments. It is less optimal for heavy database operations, parallelized compilation, or large language model inference.
